text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Two people sent to evict residents and demolish shanties in slum village of Soweto in Nairobi are killed by mob.
- Deadline for getting new-generation identity cards extended by a month, to end of February.
- Man who burned wife to death sentenced to hang.
- National Assembly speaker declares Langata seat in Nairobi vacant; Electoral Commission sets by-election for March 11.

- Opposition FORD-Asili secretary-general Martin Shikuku criticises government for involving private sector in importing maize, saying it is duty of government to import food and distribute it freely to starving families throughout country.
- High Court sentences woman who killed her lover to one-day jail term after plea of guilty.
- Government unveils ambitious 20-year programme aimed at transforming postal and telecommunications sector to more efficient, reliable and affordable service industry.
- Political woes facing abrasive cabinet minister William ole Ntimama have origin in his stubborn defiance of President Moi's instructions to reconcile with Vice-President George Saitoti.

- Clearing business tycoon Ketan Somaia of controversial 400 million shilling government contract by opposition FORD-Kenya party chairman Michael Kijana Wamalwa has brought Wamalwa into international focus concerning his honesty and transparency.
